children.value: A Career You Can Count On
In healthcare, one thing never changes: the need for CNAs. It's an exciting career opportunity with real job security, steady demand, and room to grow. The career that always needs you. Start today.

inventory.text: Career Seekers Find Your Calling with a Career in Healthcare You care about people, and that strength can become a meaningful career. As a Certified Nurse Assistant (CNA), you'll turn that passion into a stable career in healthcare, caring for seniors in long-term care while finding real opportunities to grow professionally. The Certified Nurse Assistant Program (CNAP) website has all the resources you need to take that first step. Start Your New Career Find a Training Provider Where are you in your career journey I am considering a new career in healthcare Learn About CNAs and Long-Term Care I am looking for CNA training Find a Training Provider Near You I am looking to earn a wage while I train Learn About the Earn and Learn Program Certified Nurse Assistant More than a job. A career with purpose. As a CNA, you’ll provide hands-on care for seniors and people with disabilities in skilled nursing facilities across California. This role is a great first step toward a rewarding healthcare career . The U.S. senior population is growing rapidly Learn More An estimated 1.3 million people resided in nursing home facilities as of 2020 Learn More With the Certified Nurse Assistant Program (CNAP), you can Earn and Learn —start working as a CNA while getting certified. Your New Career Starts Here Subscribe * indicates required First Name * Last Name * Zip Code * Email Address * SMS Phone Number Your CNA Story - By providing your phone number, you agree to receive promotional and marketing messages, notifications, and customer service communications from Your CNA Story. Message and data rates may apply. Consent is not a condition of purchase. Message frequency varies. Text HELP for help. Text STOP to cancel. See terms . Language Preference * English Español Tiếng Việt 简体中文 Select the language you prefer to be contacted in. Sign Up today Interested in learning more? Sign up here to receive information and guidance on how to create your own CNA story — via email and/or text message. Your CNA Story Starts Here Earn and Learn Get paid to start a career. With the Earn and Learn Program, you'll receive hands-on training to become a Certified Nurse Assistant while you earn income. Build your skills. Build your future. Start your CNA journey. Built for This Your empathy is more than a personality trait. It's a professional skill and a source of real pride. As a CNA, the care you naturally give becomes the foundation of a career where your efforts are seen and rewarded. Go beyond a job. Become vital to your community. A Career You Can Count On In healthcare, one thing never changes: the need for CNAs. It's an exciting career opportunity with real job security, steady demand, and room to grow. The career that always needs you. Start today. Earned State Recognition Becoming a CNA means earning state recognition as a skilled healthcare professional. It's not just a job title. It's a credential that opens doors, gives you stability, and sets the foundation for a career with room to grow. What is long-term Care? CNAs work in different healthcare settings. Becoming a CNA gives you career flexibility and opportunities in various healthcare environments. Skilled Nursing Be part of a team providing 24/7 nursing care in licensed healthcare facilities Learn More Short Stay Rehab Help people in their therapy journey after recovering from a surgery, illness or accident. Learn More Memory Care Care for seniors with Alzheimer’s, dementia, and other types of memory problems. Learn More Career Paths in Long-Term Care Where will your new career take you? Certified Nurse Assistant The Certified Nurse Assistant (CNA) role is a vital part of senior living communities. CNAs provide hands-on compassionate care, ensuring the well-being of residents. CNAs are essential in healthcare and have opportunities for growth. Nursing Licensed Practical Nurses (LPNs) and Registered Nurses (RNs) provide professional medical care to residents with a personalized approach. Both requre professional degrees. Administration Administrators in senior living communities are responsible for overseeing the daily operations of the facility and ensuring all state and federal regulations are met. Social Services Social services personnel work with healthcare professionals to advocate for patients, support new residents in adjusting, and provide counseling. Therapy Therapists and related staff members work one-on-one with residents to improve mobility and strength. Care Coordination Care coordination staff work with new residents and their families. Their duties include admissions and customer service. Activities Activities directors and staff add a little fun to residential life. They plan and lead fun events to keep residents engaged. Support Services It takes many hands to ensure life runs smoothly in a senior care community. Laundry, maintenance, housekeeping and dietary staff members all play vital roles.
